steps.do: Build the production bundle so Lighthouse measures the real output.
Serve the built app on port 4173 in a separate terminal.
Run Lighthouse on the layout page and save the JSON report.
Read the cumulative layout shift value from the report.

K-002014.example: The layout page reports a CLS of 0.02 after an image grid loads, below the 0.1 budget. If the value is 0.25, reserve image space with width and height attributes on each img.
K-002014.check: The jq command prints a number at or below 0.1, such as 0.02.

steps.do: Build the project so the chunks are written to dist.
List every JavaScript asset larger than 50 kilobytes.
Confirm the layout panel chunk name appears in the build listing and check its size.

K-002015.check: The find command prints no lines, and the LayoutPanel chunk is listed under 50 KB in ls -l.

steps.do: Create the tests folder if it is missing.
Create the spec file, then write a Playwright test that opens the page with 10000 rows and asserts the rendered row locator count is less than 60, using expect with a timeout.
Run the Playwright test file for the grid.

K-002016.example: With 10000 items and a 600px viewport of 40px rows, the test expects about 15 to 30 rendered rows, so it asserts toBeLessThan(60). A count of 10000 means v-for is rendering every item.
K-002016.check: The output reads '1 passed' and the locator count assertion succeeds.
traps: Counting the data array length instead of rendered DOM nodes proves nothing. Count the rendered row elements with a locator.
Playwright waits only for the first paint, so call expect with a timeout and not a fixed sleep.

steps.do: Create the tests folder if it is missing.
Create the spec file, then write a Vitest test that mounts LayoutGrid five times with @vue/test-utils, measures each mount with performance.now, and asserts the median is less than 200 milliseconds.
Run the Vitest file once.

K-002017.example: The test mounts LayoutGrid with 200 cards and records a median of 84ms, passing the 200ms limit. A median of 412ms means a computed property or watcher is recalculating on every mount.
K-002017.check: The output reads 'Tests 1 passed' and the measured median is under 200.
traps: Jsdom does not lay out the page, so this checks script cost only, not paint. Use Playwright for real layout timing.
Run the mount measurement more than once and compare the median, since the first run includes module loading.

steps.do: Confirm the onUpdated counter exists in the child layout component and is exposed to the test through a prop or emitted event.
Create the tests folder if it is missing.
Create the spec file, then write a Vitest test that changes one unrelated parent ref once, awaits nextTick, and asserts the child counter equals 0.
Run the test to confirm the counter stays at 0 after the unrelated change.

K-002018.example: Changing the sidebarOpen ref should not re-render the grid child, so the counter stays at 0. If it reads 3, pass the grid a memoized prop with a v-memo directive or move the state into a shallowRef.
K-002018.check: The output reads 'Tests 1 passed' and the asserted render count equals 0.
traps: Counting renders by logging inside the template is noisy. Use an onUpdated hook counter instead.
Vue batches updates within one tick, so change the ref once per test and await nextTick before reading the counter.

steps.do: Confirm the component pairs each observe call with a disconnect call in onBeforeUnmount.
Create the tests folder if it is missing.

Create the spec file, then write a Vitest test that sets a spy on window.ResizeObserver before mounting, counts observe and disconnect calls, unmounts the wrapper, and asserts both counts are equal and at least 1.
Run the test file.

K-002019.example: The spy records observe 1 and disconnect 1 after unmount, so the test passes. If disconnect stays at 0, the observer was created in onMounted without a matching onBeforeUnmount cleanup.
K-002019.check: The output reads 'Tests 1 passed' with observe and disconnect counts both equal to 1.
traps: Creating the observer in setup but never disconnecting it causes a leak after each route change. Pair each observe with a disconnect in onBeforeUnmount.
A spy on the wrong global object passes silently, so set the spy on window.ResizeObserver before mounting.

steps.do: Confirm the root layout file exists before editing it.
Add an anchor with href #main and the classes sr-only and focus:not-sr-only before the nav element.
Give the main element id main and tabIndex -1 so focus moves into the content.
Add a Playwright test that presses Tab once and asserts the skip link is focused and visible.
Run the skip link test.
Run axe on the home page for bypass rule violations.

K-002020.example: The skip link is Skip to content as the first child of body. On Tab it appears 1rem from the top and left edges, since left-4 and top-4 equal 1rem.
K-002020.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and axe exits with code 0 with no bypass-blocks violation listed.
traps: Using hidden or display none instead of sr-only removes the link from keyboard focus entirely.
Forgetting focus:not-sr-only keeps the link invisible even when it is focused.
Leaving main without tabIndex -1 means the skip link lands focus on a non-focusable element.

steps.do: Confirm the nav component file exists.
Read the current pathname in the nav and compare it with each link href.
Set aria-current to 'page' only on the matching link and leave it undefined on the others.
Add aria-[current=page]:font-semibold and aria-[current=page]:underline to the link classes.
Give every link the classes min-h-11 and min-w-11 so each target is at least 44px square.
Count aria-current lines in the nav to confirm the active-state logic is present.
Run the Playwright test that visits /docs and asserts exactly one link has aria-current page.

K-002021.example: On /docs the link renders with aria-current='page' and gains font-semibold through the aria-[current=page]:font-semibold class. Its box uses min-h-11 and min-w-11, which is 2.75rem or 44px per side, meeting the 44px target size guideline.
K-002021.check: grep prints 1 and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Setting aria-current='true' is valid but less specific than 'page', so use 'page' for navigation links.
Showing the active state only through color hides it from users who cannot perceive the difference.
The aria-[current=page] variant needs Tailwind 3.2 or newer.

steps.do: Count md: classes in the nav to confirm the collapse breakpoint is in use.
Add a useState hook for open with the initial value false.
Render a button with type button, aria-controls mobile-menu, and aria-expanded bound to the open state.
Put aria-expanded:rotate-180 on the chevron svg so it flips when the menu is open.
Give the mobile panel id mobile-menu and the classes md:hidden plus hidden when closed.
Run the Playwright test that clicks the toggle and checks aria-expanded changes from false to true.

K-002022.example: A closed toggle renders aria-expanded='false' and aria-controls='mobile-menu' with className='md:hidden min-h-11 min-w-11 p-2'. After one click React sets aria-expanded='true' and the panel loses its hidden class.
K-002022.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the grep count is at least 2.
traps: Using a div with onClick instead of a real button removes built-in keyboard support.
Forgetting aria-controls leaves assistive technology unable to link the button to the panel.
Leaving aria-expanded unset instead of binding it to state means the open or closed status is never announced.

steps.do: Search the nav file for outline-none that would remove keyboard focus.
Replace each removed outline with focus-visible:outline-2 and focus-visible:outline-offset-2.
Set the ring color to focus-visible:outline-blue-700 so it has at least 3:1 contrast against white.
Use focus-visible instead of focus so mouse clicks do not draw the ring.
Count outline-none matches again and expect none.
Run axe with the wcag21aa tags to catch non-text contrast and focus violations.

K-002023.example: A link with focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-blue-700 draws a 2px blue ring with a 2px gap when Tab reaches it. A mouse click on the same link draws no ring, so pointer users see no change.
K-002023.check: The second grep prints 0 and exits with code 1, and axe exits with code 0.
traps: Choosing a light color such as blue-200 fails the 3:1 threshold on white.
Using focus instead of focus-visible draws rings on every mouse click.
Leaving outline-none in place removes the only visible focus signal.

steps.do: Count transition lines in the nav to find motion that needs gating.
Add motion-reduce:transition-none and motion-reduce:transform-none to the drawer panel classes.
Keep duration-200 on the drawer so users without the setting get a 200ms slide.
Add a Playwright test that emulates reduced motion and reads the drawer transition-duration.
Run the reduced-motion test.
Count motion-reduce lines to confirm the variant is applied.

K-002024.example: The drawer uses className='transition duration-200 motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none' so a default user sees a 200ms slide. With prefers-reduced-motion set to reduce, its computed transition-duration reads 0s.
K-002024.check: Playwright prints '2 passed' for the normal and reduced cases, and the grep count is at least 1.
traps: Writing only a motion-reduce variant without the base transition class gives the override nothing to change.
Forgetting motion-reduce:transform-none leaves transform animations running.
Assuming the OS dark mode setting controls motion is wrong, since it only controls prefers-color-scheme.

steps.do: Count nav elements in the components folder to see how many landmarks exist.
Give the header nav aria-label Primary and the footer nav aria-label Footer.
Check that the aria-label values across the source are unique for each nav.
Run axe with the best-practice tag to check the landmark-unique rule.
Run a Playwright test that lists navigation landmarks and expects the names Primary and Footer.

K-002025.example: The header renders <nav aria-label='Primary'> and the footer renders <nav aria-label='Footer'>, so screen readers list two named navigation landmarks. The Playwright query getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Primary' }) should match exactly one element.
K-002025.check: grep shows the two distinct labels, axe exits with code 0 with no landmark-unique violation, and Playwright prints '1 passed'.

An aria-labelledby pointing to a missing id gives the landmark no name.
Adding role='navigation' to a div duplicates the landmark that the nav element already provides.

steps.do: Confirm the skeleton markup uses the animate-pulse utility in the tabs component.
Run the Playwright spec that mocks a 200ms data delay for the tabs.
In the spec, assert that the skeleton locator has count 0 after the active tab panel is visible, without a fixed sleep.
Re-run the spec with the grep flag to confirm the empty-state path also clears the skeleton.

K-002026.example: The spec makes the tab data route respond after 200ms and expects the locator [data-testid="tab-skeleton"] to have count 0 once the Overview panel is visible. Playwright reports 1 passed for the loading test.
K-002026.check: The rg command prints at least one line from Tabs.tsx, and Playwright prints '2 passed' with no failed tests.

steps.do: Find where aria-busy is set in the tabs component.
Read the component test to confirm aria-busy is true while loading and false after the fetch resolves.
Run the component unit test that checks aria-busy changes across a tab switch.
Count the lines that declare role tabpanel to confirm one per tab.

K-002027.example: When the Reports tab is clicked, the panel renders with aria-busy="true" and a pulse skeleton, then switches to aria-busy="false" when the fetch resolves. The Vitest run reports 3 tests passed for the switch sequence.
K-002027.check: Vitest prints 'Tests 3 passed', and rg -c returns the number of tabs, for example 4 for four tabs.
traps: Small models often put aria-busy on the tab button instead of the tabpanel. Put it on the element with role tabpanel.
The value must be the string true or false. Do not write aria-busy='yes'.

steps.do: Build the stylesheet with the Tailwind v4 CLI from the entry CSS file.
Count animate-pulse rules in the compiled CSS.
Count motion-reduce variant rules in the compiled CSS.
Check the compiled file size in bytes so no unused utilities leaked in.

K-002028.example: The compiled file contains .animate-pulse and a motion-reduce:animate-none rule, and stat prints 18432 bytes. Both rg counts return at least 1.
K-002028.check: Each rg count is 1 or more, and stat prints a number below 50000.
traps: Tailwind v4 uses @import "tailwindcss" in the entry CSS, not the v3 @tailwind directives. Mixing them drops utilities.
If a count is 0, the source path is not scanned. Check the content globs in tailwind.config.js for v3, or the @source line in src/index.css for v4.

steps.do: Start the Vite dev server so the tabs page is reachable on port 5173.
Hold the tabs data request open with the test route so the loading state stays on screen.
Run axe against the tabs page and fail on any violation.
Check that any skeleton or loading text meets 4.5:1 contrast by reading the color-contrast rule in the axe output.

K-002029.example: Axe scans /tabs while the Settings panel is pending, and the color-contrast rule passes for gray-500 text on white at 4.83:1. The scan exits with status 0.
K-002029.check: axe exits 0 and prints no violations, and the color-contrast result shows a ratio of 4.5:1 or higher.
traps: Axe only checks what is on screen, so the scan must run during loading, not after it ends.
Do not lower the contrast threshold to pass. Keep 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

steps.do: Create the reports directory for the audit output.
Run Lighthouse on the tabs page for the accessibility category only.
Read the accessibility score from the JSON report.
Confirm the score is at least 0.9 and record the number in the pull request.

K-002030.example: Lighthouse writes reports/tabs.json, and jq prints 0.96 for the accessibility score on the tabs route. That value is above the 0.9 gate.
K-002030.check: jq prints a number of 0.9 or higher, and 1 means every audit passed.
traps: Lighthouse needs the dev server running on localhost:5173 first, or it audits an error page. A score of 0 usually means the page did not load.
Read the accessibility score field, not the performance field, when checking this gate.

steps.do: Confirm the tab buttons declare role tab in the component.
Run the Vitest keyboard test that presses ArrowRight while a panel is loading.
Read the test to confirm the second tab has aria-selected true and tabIndex 0 after one ArrowRight press.
Run the Playwright keyboard spec to confirm focus moves with the arrow keys in a real browser.

K-002031.example: The test focuses the Overview tab during a 200ms load, presses ArrowRight, and expects Reports to have aria-selected="true" and tabIndex 0. Vitest reports 2 tests passed.
K-002031.check: Vitest prints 'Tests 2 passed', and Playwright prints '1 passed' with no timeouts.
traps: Small models move focus but forget roving tabindex, which needs tabIndex -1 on inactive tabs. Test both aria-selected and tabindex.
Do not disable the arrow key handler while loading. Keyboard users still need to move between tabs.

steps.do: Confirm the chart tokens are declared in the theme file.
Build the Tailwind CSS output from the input file.
Count the generated chart label utility rules in the built CSS.
Check the label size token resolves to 0.75rem in the built CSS.

K-002032.example: The block in src/styles/input.css sets --text-chart-label: 0.75rem and --text-chart-label--line-height: 1rem, so the build must emit a .text-chart-label rule. The rg count prints at least 2 and the value line prints 0.75rem, so the token works.
K-002032.check: rg -cF prints a count of at least 2 (the variable and the class rule), and the rg -nF line shows --text-chart-label: 0.75rem; with its line number.
traps: Writing text-[12px] in chart JSX passes the build but skips the token.
Tailwind v4 reads @theme in the CSS file, not tailwind.config.js, so a config-only token never makes a utility.
Skipping the rebuild makes the counts check a stale dist/app.css.

steps.do: List the chart component files that may contain styling.
Search chart components for raw hex color literals.
Search chart components for arbitrary value classes such as text-[13px].
Search chart components for inline style objects that bypass tokens.

K-002033.example: A chart file with fill='#2563eb' on line 41 prints src/components/chart/Bar.tsx:41, so the fix swaps it for fill-chart-2. After the change the same search prints nothing.
K-002033.check: All three searches print no lines once every value is a token.
traps: Searching only for six-digit hex misses three-digit and eight-digit forms, so use the pattern given.
rgb(), hsl() and inline style objects bypass tokens and need their own search.
A match in a comment or test fixture is a false positive, so read each file and line before editing.

steps.do: Start the dev server in a separate terminal and leave it running.
Run the Playwright spec that measures rendered tick label metrics.
Confirm the spec asserts a minimum computed font size.
Confirm the spec asserts tabular numerals on tick values.

K-002034.example: The spec loads /charts/revenue at 320px and 1280px wide, then reads getComputedStyle on each [data-chart-tick] element and expects a fontSize of at least 12px. It also expects fontVariantNumeric to equal tabular-nums, which the tabular-nums class sets.
K-002034.check: Playwright reports 0 failed with at least 1 passed, and both rg searches print one matching line each.
traps: Reading class names instead of computed style proves nothing, so assert on getComputedStyle.
A 12px label can still clip on a 320px mobile chart, so run the spec at both widths.
The tests fail with connection errors if the dev server is not running first.

steps.do: Start the dev server if it is not already running.
Run axe on the chart page against WCAG 2.1 AA rules and exit nonzero on any violation.
Confirm the axis label color token is declared in the theme file.
Confirm the axis labels use the token class rather than a raw color.

K-002035.example: The token --color-chart-axis is #6b7280 on the white #ffffff background, which measures about 4.8:1 and passes the 4.5:1 text minimum. In dark mode a #4b5563 value on #111827 measures about 2.3:1, so axe reports a color-contrast violation with the failing node.
K-002035.check: axe reports zero violations and exits with code 0, and the two rg searches each print at least one line.
traps: Checking only the light theme misses dark-mode token overrides, so run axe in both themes.
axe can pass an empty chart, so confirm the SVG rendered before trusting exit code 0.
Some checks skip SVG text drawn with fill, so verify the color pair by hand against the 4.5:1 minimum.

steps.do: List the series color tokens declared in the theme file.
Confirm each series bar uses a fill token class.
Run the Playwright spec that computes fill against plot background contrast.
Confirm the spec asserts the 3:1 non-text minimum.

K-002036.example: The spec reads getComputedStyle(bar).fill for each [data-series] bar and the plot background, then computes the WCAG ratio. --color-chart-2 #2563eb on #ffffff measures about 5.2:1 and passes, while #93c5fd on #ffffff measures about 1.8:1 and fails the 3:1 minimum.
K-002036.check: Playwright reports one passed line per series and 0 failed, and the last rg search prints the assertion line.
traps: A pale tint can look distinct on screen and still fall under 3:1, so measure the ratio instead of judging by eye.
Series told apart by hue alone fail for color-blind readers, so add a pattern or direct label.
Measuring against the page background instead of the plot area gives the wrong ratio.

steps.do: Count light theme declarations of the series token in the source.
Build the Tailwind CSS output.
Count the series token declarations in the built CSS.
Confirm the dark selector block exists in the built CSS.
Run the Playwright spec that toggles the theme and compares fill colors.

K-002037.example: src/styles/input.css declares --color-chart-1: #2563eb in :root and --color-chart-1: #60a5fa inside .dark, so both counts print 2. If the built count prints 1, the build dropped the dark override, and the .dark search shows which block is missing.
K-002037.check: Both token counts print 2, one from :root and one from .dark, the .dark search prints its line, and Playwright reports 0 failed.
traps: Counting declarations in source proves nothing about what ships, so count in dist/app.css too.
Recoloring with a dark: utility in JSX can leave SVG fill values unchanged, so override the token instead.
A dark value that passes in light mode can fall below 3:1 against the dark background, so measure it again.

steps.do: Create the composables folder if it is missing.
In src/composables/useToast.ts, declare const MAX_VISIBLE = 3, a module-level const visible = shallowRef<Toast[]>([]), and a module-level const queue of Toast items outside the exported function.
Export useToast() with a push function that appends to visible when its length is below MAX_VISIBLE and otherwise appends to queue.
Run the Vue type checker on the project.
Confirm the cap constant is declared in the composable file.

K-002038.check: grep prints a line like 4:const MAX_VISIBLE = 3, and vue-tsc exits 0 with no output.

Forgetting to shift from queue when a toast closes leaves toasts stuck forever.
Setting MAX_VISIBLE to a non-number breaks the length check.

steps.do: In src/components/ToastContainer.vue, wrap the v-for list in TransitionGroup with tag set to div and name set to toast.
Use the toast id as the v-for key, never the array index.
Add CSS for the toast-leave-active class with position absolute so remaining toasts slide without moving the whole stack.
Run eslint on the container file.
Count how many lines in the container use toast.id.

K-002039.check: eslint exits 0 with no output, and grep -c prints 2 or more.

steps.do: In src/App.vue, wrap the ToastContainer component in Teleport with the to prop set to body.
Mount ToastContainer once in App.vue and not inside any routed page, so it is created one time.
Run the spec that mounts the app and counts toast host nodes.
Count the Teleport usages in the source tree to confirm there is exactly one host.

K-002040.check: vitest reports 1 passed, and grep lists exactly one Teleport line in src/App.vue.

Teleporting to a selector that does not exist at mount time logs a warning and renders nothing.

Start a setTimeout of 4000 milliseconds for each toast and store its returned id in the Map under the toast id.
In src/components/Toast.vue, call onBeforeUnmount to clearTimeout the stored id for that toast.
Run the spec that fires a toast and advances fake timers by 4000 milliseconds.
Confirm clearTimeout is called in the toast component.

K-002041.check: vitest reports 1 passed, and grep prints a line containing clearTimeout with the stored id.

steps.do: In src/components/ToastContainer.vue, add v-memo to the v-for item element with the array holding toast.id, toast.message, and toast.closing.
Keep the v-memo dependency array limited to the fields that change the rendered output.
Run eslint on the container file to check the directive usage.
Run the render benchmark spec that mounts 50 toasts and times one update.
Confirm the v-memo directive appears in the template.

K-002042.check: vitest reports 1 passed under the 16 millisecond assertion, and grep prints one line containing v-memo.

Replace each individual visible.value push with one assignment of the full next array during the flush.
Run the spec that pushes 20 toasts in the same tick and expects one flush.
Confirm queueMicrotask is used in the composable.
Run the Vue type checker to confirm the batching types compile.

K-002043.example: Pushing 20 toasts in one tick makes exactly 1 assignment to visible.value, which a spy on the ref setter counts. The spec expects that count to equal 1.
K-002043.check: vitest reports 1 passed, grep prints the queueMicrotask line, and vue-tsc exits 0.

steps.do: Create the Modals folder under Sources for the sheet views.
Create LoadingSheet.swift in that folder.
Declare @State private var isLoading = false, set it to true before the await call, and reset it in defer so it clears after a thrown error too.
Replace the submit label with ProgressView while isLoading is true, and add .disabled(isLoading) to the Button that starts the request.
Confirm the sheet file exists.
Count disabled modifiers in the file, expecting at least 1.

K-002044.check: test -f exits 0 with no output, and grep -c prints 1 or higher, showing the disabled modifier is present.

steps.do: Add .interactiveDismissDisabled(isLoading) to the sheet content so the swipe-down gesture is blocked while the request runs.
Confirm the modifier appears exactly once in the sheet file.
Count references to isLoading, expecting at least 3 for the declaration, the disabled call, and the dismiss guard.
List the lines that reference isLoading with their line numbers.

K-002045.check: grep -c interactiveDismissDisabled prints 1, and grep -c isLoading prints 3 or higher.

steps.do: Create ProfileSheet.swift in the Modals folder.
Start a task that calls Task.sleep for .milliseconds(200), then sets showSkeleton to true only if the load has not finished.
Apply .redacted(reason: .placeholder) to the content rows while showSkeleton is true.
Confirm the 200ms delay call is present.
